patch.value: pm gantt refuses to run on any tracker that uses symmetric related links, because cycle detection ignores the dependency kind

detectCycles walked every dependency edge regardless of kind. A related edge is symmetric and pm records it on both items, so each mutually-related pair is a two-node cycle, and the command treats a cycle as a fatal data problem and refuses to render. Against the companion tracker of 664 real items this produced four fatal dependency cycles and no chart at all, none of them an ordering. gatingDepIds also excluded only related, relates_to and duplicate, so the related_to spelling that real trackers emit was treated as a scheduling dependency in the scheduler as well.

value.author: codex
value.text: Found by running the built extension against a copy of the companion's real tracker rather than by reading the code. The unit tests all passed and the coverage gate read 100/100/100 while the command could not render a single chart on a real dataset. That is the gap between per-function coverage and end-to-end usability, and only real data exposed it.

value.author: codex
value.text: Fixed by naming the non-gating kinds explicitly and applying the same predicate in both places. The set is derived from what fleet trackers actually emit, counted across all repositories: related 5161, implements 2124, discovered_from 370, parent 340, blocks 226, verifies 167, blocked_by 146, supersedes 60, related_to 53, child 8. The kinds that annotate a relationship rather than order work are excluded; blocked_by, blocks and implements still gate.

value.author: codex
value.text: A larger design question is deliberately left open rather than folded in here. The filter is a DENYLIST, so any kind not listed counts as a scheduling dependency, which means implements at 2124 uses and blocks at 226 currently order the work. An allowlist of genuinely gating kinds would be more defensible, but it changes every computed schedule in every consumer, so it needs its own change and its own review rather than riding along in a coverage pull request.

message: Filter cycle detection to gating dependency kinds

value.author: codex
value.text: First review of this pull request found that the gating predicate had been applied to only two of five dependency traversals. detectCycles and gatingDepIds used it; computeCriticalPath filtered nothing at all, and computeSchedule and computeSlack each kept a local three-kind denylist. So related_to, parent, child, supersedes and discovered_from were excluded from cycle detection and the JSON export while still ordering the work through scheduling, slack and the critical path - one command interpreting the same graph two different ways, which is arguably worse than the original bug because the two answers disagree.

value.author: codex
value.text: That is the same frame error recorded on the pm-rl work earlier today: fix the sites where a defect surfaced rather than every consumer of the value. Here the defect surfaced in cycle detection, I fixed cycle detection and the exported helper, and left three traversals reading the graph the old way. All five now share one isGatingDep, covered by a parameterized test asserting that each of the ten non-gating kinds orders nothing in either computeSchedule or computeCriticalPath, with blocked_by as the control that still does both.

value.author: codex
value.text: Three test-quality findings in the same review, all real. A progress assertion selected an item with startsWith pm- and asserted only that something was found, so it passed whatever the closed item's percentage was; it now selects the closed task by id, asserts 100, and asserts the in-progress task is below 100 so the field is shown to vary with status. A test named returns an empty set for a cyclic graph asserted a size of 2, so the name and the assertion contradicted each other; the guard stops recursive re-entry without discarding the chain walked to reach it, and the name now says that. And two glyph assertions matched the whole ASCII output, which always contains a legend listing every glyph - those assertions could never fail and are now scoped to the rendered row.
